books.section: Topic 4.10 The Second Great Awakening, Utopian Communities

stimulus.text: Two utopian communities tried to rebuild American life from scratch. Brook Farm, founded outside Boston in 1841 by the transcendentalist George Ripley, shared labor equally among its members and valued leisure as a way of becoming fuller human beings. New Harmony, founded in Indiana in 1825 by the Scottish industrialist Robert Owen, was built on principles of total equality. Both drew on European thinkers: Brook Farm on the French socialist Charles Fourier, New Harmony on Owen himself.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 6, Topic 4.10, Utopian Communities: Brook Farm established outside Boston in 1841 by George Ripley, equal sharing of labor and leisure; New Harmony founded by Robert Owen in 1825 around total equality; inspiration from Fourier and Owen. Original synthesis, not a quotation.

source: original; stimulus paraphrases Barron's on Brook Farm and New Harmony
stem: New Harmony and Brook Farm are best compared as which of the following?

options.text: Two Southern plantations that defended slavery as a positive good
options.misconception: Southern plantations defended slavery then, so any communal settlement can look like a plantation.

options.text: Two experiments in communal living inspired by European socialist thinkers
Two federal military forts built to defend the western frontier
options.misconception: Forts defended the frontier then, so a settlement in Indiana can look like a military post.

options.text: Two banks founded to issue paper money for western settlers
options.misconception: Banks issued paper money then, so a new institution can look like a bank.

rationales.A: Both communities were northern experiments in equality, not Southern plantations, and neither defended slavery.
rationales.B: Brook Farm drew on the French socialist Fourier, New Harmony on the Scot Robert Owen. Both were European-inspired communal experiments.
rationales.C: Neither was a fort. New Harmony was a town in Indiana built on equality, and Brook Farm was a farm commune outside Boston.
rationales.D: Neither issued money or lent it. Both were communities trying to live differently, not banks serving settlers.
rationales.general:
1. Ask what the two share: both were communities built on shared labor and equality, not on wages.
2. Ask where the ideas came from: Fourier in France for Brook Farm, Owen in Scotland for New Harmony.
3. Name the pair: European socialist thought, tried out as American communal living.
Background: New Harmony was founded by Robert Owen himself in 1825 around principles of total equality.
Remember: when two experiments share a foreign idea, the idea is the story, not the address.
